Coverage

How to read this map

View mode (top-right) switches what colors the map:
• Data — pick a factor from the list to color every tract & substation by that raw value: headroom, winter growth, households, PLUTO residential units / commercial area, outages per 1k, heat vulnerability, heat-pump adoption, DAC, or the Step-3 priority frequency (how often it lands in the top 20% across 4,000 random factor weightings). This view is static — the budget does nothing here.
• Investment — colors by the $ each asset needs, and activates the budget.

Investment target — the paper's two leveling versions:
• Balancing — raise every below-standard asset toward its peer-median per-household headroom (network median for a transformer, citywide median for a substation), with each program step capped at 5% of asset size. The budget slider spans the full leveling bill: $4.75B by wire (about $6.3B by battery — deep cuts favor wires); the paper's headline first step (5%) costs $0.73B wire / $0.39B battery.
• Growth — the same leveling on the growth-adjusted headroom (ĥ = h − 15-yr winter growth), so assets eroded by electrification need more. Full bill $5.1B wire / $7.2B battery. (The paper's business-as-usual benchmark — host just +5% — costs only $0.12B, shown in each popup.)

Technology — the budget can buy Wire ($700/kW transformer, $2,000/kW substation) or Battery ($500/kWh in homes). Battery energy follows the measured load shapes: a 5% shave needs about 2.3 hours of discharge, and tract batteries relieve their substation for free (double duty). Batteries win the shallow regime; wires win deep repairs.

Budget slider funds assets in priority order across both layers, with the chosen technology, up to the dollar amount. Reveal by budget hides what isn't funded yet. Each popup's status tells you whether that asset is funded (for the current target & technology) at the current budget, and the budget it enters at.

Layers. Transformer (underground, solid warm YlOrRd), Feeder (overhead radial, dashed-white outline) and Substation (violet cyan-dashed regions) toggle independently and use separate color ramps.

Clicking. Click layer chooses whether clicks hit tracts or substations. Each popup shows every factor value, the per-layer wire & 2-hour-battery investment for the chosen target, the funding status, and the priority rank (e.g. 15 / 2,279). The Data table tab lists all substations and tracts, sortable.
